contexts.text: In the antediluvians (this seed) was extinguished by tares.
The tares () = evils and falsities. ( = falsity. AC 7571.) ( = the falsities and evils of the former Church. TCR 784:end.)
The sons of the evil kingdom, who are the tares = the falsities of faith of the Church.
The evils (in man) are tares, which strike wide roots, and obstruct the roots of the good seed.

Unless there are the Truths of faith... there are the roots of tares, which obstruct (the truths and goods inseminated by the Lord); but still they do not exstirpate them; for they are reserved, so that while the tares are taking root, they are produced, and grow.
If there are falsities in the ideas, they must be eradicated; for they are like tares...

The Lord compares the Kingdom of God... to a man gathering tares... This is presented to view in the other life. (Fully described under Ferment, here.) This is the gathering of the tares into bundles.

(The parable of the tares) treats of the Last Judgment, when there must be a separation of the good from the evil... While men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares, and went his way = that with natural men the falsities of evil inflow from Hell, and are received... Tares = the evil of falsity, and thus those who are in evil through falsities. ( = evils, or those in whom evils are. AE 397:2.) ( = the evil. AE 426:3.) ( = infernal falsity. AE 683:6.) ( = the falsities of doctrine, of religion, and of worship, which are from evil; and therefore they are called the sons of the evil. AE 740:5) ( = the evil, who at the Last Judgment will be cast into Hell. AE 849:2.)
(Why the tares were to be allowed to grow until the time of harvest.) AE 426:3. AE 624:3. AE 911:2. AE 911:7.

While men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares = that while men are leading a natural life, or a life of the world, then evils from Hell secretly, or while they are unconscious of it, insinuate and implant falsities... When the blade sprang up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also = that when truth grew and produced good, falsities from evil were intermingled with it... Lord wilt thou that we... gather up the tares? = the separation and casting out of falsities from evil before truths from good are received and increase. Nay, lest haply while ye gather up the tares, ye root up the wheat with them = that so truth from good, and its increase, would also perish. For, with the men of the Church, truths are intermingled with falsities, and these cannot be separated... until they are reformed. (Further explained.) The tares are the sons of the evil = the falsities with those who are in evil.
